rounds.reviewer: claude-opus-5-5 (critique agent, separate from the builder)

problems.what: scene text keeps growing after it has been read and is sliced by the frame edges and the caption plate: 'eryone fr' across the top, a 150 px 'Th[plate]pm' flanking 'and finds the hour for everyone.', 'Standup', 'Offsite' and 'Thu 14' cut in half at the edges; the fragments fight the caption at phone size
problems.fix: set every in-scene word to dissolve, as a pure function of where it sits on screen, before a frame edge, the tag or the caption plate can cut it

problems.what: the phone's app bar ('Oriel', the Day/Week/Month control) and then the 'Thu 14' header slide under the ORIEL tag: two Oriel names stacked in one corner and a header half hidden
problems.fix: the same keep-out: scene text fades as it nears the tag's plate, so only shapes pass behind it

problems.what: the hook is a dark plum slab: the centre tower's grey window grid is as loud as the one lit window it is about to enter, so the eye has no single target in the first two seconds
problems.fix: quiet the tower's other windows toward the ink and give the lit window a warm glow on the facade so frame 0 has one focus

problems.what: one continuous glide: critique.mjs counts 0 abrupt changes in 10 s and a 20 s calm; the key word's pop is the only punch
problems.fix: a punch on each key-word tick inside the scene (for example the free hour's ring snapping), keyed to the global frame so the loop and the hand-offs stay exact

problems.what: between two captions the white plate is empty or shows only a stray comma for a few frames
problems.fix: minor; it is the roll between captions and lasts under half a second

rounds.reviewer: claude-opus-5-5 (critique agent, separate from the builder)

problems.what: the app bar's Day/Week/Month pill still passes behind the ORIEL tag (its words are gone, only the shape remains)
problems.fix: none needed; the tag sits on its own plate and shapes passing under it read as depth

problems.what: a dissolving word ('Thu 14', 'Thu 14 · 2–3 pm') is half transparent for a few frames
problems.fix: none needed; it is the dissolve, and reads better than the slice it replaces

problems.what: critique.mjs still counts 0 abrupt changes: a Droste push never cuts, and the tick punches are small in area
problems.fix: none; each level now lands a punch on its tick, which is what the variety criterion asks of a deliberate one-shot push

problems.what: the plate is nearly empty for 3-4 frames while the next caption starts to rise in (it is no longer oversized)
problems.fix: none needed; it is the roll between captions

fixed: every in-scene word dissolves, as a pure function of its on-screen box, before a frame edge, the ORIEL tag or the caption plate can cut it (the keep-out is a module-level record rebuilt from the layout at the top of every paint, before the zoom reads it): no more 'eryone fr', 'Th[plate]pm', half 'Standup'/'Offsite', or 'Thu 14'/'Oriel'/'Day' under the tag; 'Everyone free' is whole and readable from about 00:14.6 as the chip grows and starts to dissolve at about 00:16.2

the hook: the centre tower's windows are quieted toward the ink and the lit window carries a warm glow on the facade, so frame 0 has one focus; each caption now rises in over the last 12 frames of the level before it and is whole on the hand-off, so frame 0 opens on a complete line in a plate sized to it (the oversized plate at the start of each level is gone)

variety: a punch on every key-word tick, keyed to the global frame with a 120-frame period so the loop and hand-offs stay exact: the window glow flares (00:00.5), the lamp flicker now starts on the tick (00:04.5), a violet ring snaps out of the free hour (00:08.5 small, 00:12.5 full frame), the four avatars hop (00:16.5), and the key word jumps and settles on each tick

checks.handOffs: steps at frames 120/240/360/480 equal their neighbours in both sizes (vertical 24.3/18.2/21.4/13.9 %, landscape 23.7/17.5/27.8/13.6 %); the largest inner steps are the tick punches at frames 15-18, on purpose

notes: variety 8 is a judgment against critique.mjs's 0 changes per 10 s: a Droste push never cuts, so the count stays 0; each level now lands a punch on its tick

caption timing now differs from the brief's wording: captions rise in over the previous level's last 12 frames and are whole on the hand-off (the brief says over the first beat of the level); the key word still lands on the tick
